metadata.title: Implement Automatic Rescheduling for Missed Study Sessions

story.iWant: my study plan to automatically adjust when I mark a session as 'Missed'
story.soThat: my schedule remains realistic and I can stay on track without manual effort.
story.tasks: - Enhance the frontend's `updateSessionStatus` handler to make a `fire-and-forget` call to `POST /reschedule-plan` when a session is marked 'Missed'. - Pass `course_id` and `reason: "TASK_MISSED"` in the request body. - Implement the `POST /reschedule-plan` endpoint in the FastAPI Backend. - Verify user authorization for the given `course_id`. - Fetch all 'Not Started' study sessions for the course. - Implement the core rescheduling algorithm to redistribute tasks. - Perform a bulk `UPDATE` on `scheduled_date` for affected `study_sessions` in Supabase. - Ensure the backend rescheduling algorithm completes within performance requirements (< 5 seconds). - Implement robust error handling and logging for the rescheduling process in the backend.

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: 1. When a user marks a study session as 'Missed' in the frontend, the remaining 'Not Started' sessions for that course are automatically rescheduled by the backend (AC1 from Tech Spec). - The rescheduling logic prioritizes distributing tasks evenly across available time slots before the exam date.

constraint.description: The rescheduling algorithm on the backend must complete in under 5 seconds, even for a course with hundreds of study sessions.
The algorithm should be optimized to minimize the number of database queries (fetch upfront, calculate in memory, bulk update).
The `/reschedule-plan` endpoint must be protected and verify that the requesting user owns the `course_id`.
The rescheduling algorithm must be transactional. If any part of it fails, the user's study plan should not be left in a corrupted or partially updated state.
Log the execution time of the rescheduling algorithm. If the algorithm fails, log the error with `course_id` and plan state.
The rescheduling algorithm must only operate on study sessions with a status of 'Not Started' or 'Missed'.

tests.standards: Unit Tests (Backend): Create an extensive test suite for the rescheduling algorithm, covering various scenarios such as plans with no room, ample room, many missed tasks, etc. The algorithm should be testable in isolation as a pure function. Integration Tests (Backend): Test the `/reschedule-plan` endpoint, mocking the database to provide various plan states and verifying the generated `UPDATE` queries. E2E Tests: Test the full flow of automatic rescheduling by marking a task as 'Missed' in the frontend and asserting that the calendar view updates correctly via real-time.

ideas.idea: Simulate marking a study session as 'Missed' in the frontend and verify that a call to `POST /reschedule-plan` is made with correct parameters.
Backend unit test for the rescheduling algorithm to ensure it correctly redistributes 'Not Started' sessions given various inputs (e.g., full schedule, empty slots, varied session durations).
E2E test: mark a session 'Missed', verify the dashboard updates automatically (via Realtime) to reflect the new schedule for other sessions in the same course.
Integration test the `/reschedule-plan` endpoint to ensure it properly enforces user authorization and `course_id` ownership.
Profile the rescheduling algorithm with a large dataset (e.g., 200+ sessions) to ensure it meets the <5 second performance requirement.
